step1_analysis.description: A differential delay cell typically used in a Voltage-Controlled Delay Line (VCDL) for a Delay-Locked Loop (DLL). It features a cross-coupled PMOS pair for fast transitions and full output swing, along with tunable PMOS loads controlled by a bias voltage to adjust the propagation delay.

paper_reference.title: A 500-Mb/s Quadruple Data Rate SDRAM Interface Using a Skew Cancellation Technique

propagation_delay.description: Average time delay between the differential input transitions and the corresponding output transitions.

sky130_expected.calculation: Delay ≈ C_load * VDD / I_avg. With C_load ≈ 50fF (parasitics + load) and I_avg ≈ 1mA, Delay ≈ 50fF * 1.8V / 1mA = 90ps.
sky130_expected.reasoning: SKY130 (130nm) is significantly faster than the original 0.35um process, so the intrinsic delay of a single cell will be shorter than the 250ps skew reported in the paper.

power_consumption.description: Average power consumption of the delay cell during continuous switching.

sky130_expected.calculation: P = VDD * I_avg. I_avg ≈ 0.5mA to 1mA. P ≈ 1.8V * 0.75mA = 1.35mW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The 570 mW reported is for the entire SDRAM interface. A single delay cell consumes a very small fraction of that total power.

output_swing.description: Peak-to-peak voltage swing of the output nodes.

sky130_expected.calculation: The cross-coupled PMOS pulls the high node to VDD (1.8V), and the NMOS pulls the low node to GND (0V).
sky130_expected.reasoning: The cross-coupled PMOS load ensures near rail-to-rail swing, overcoming the threshold voltage drops seen in purely diode-connected loads.

step3_testbench.description: Measures propagation delay, output voltage swing, and average power consumption of the differential delay cell under a 250 MHz (500 Mb/s) differential input stimulus.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Testbench for Differential Delay Cell
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u
.param W_xm5=5u L_xm5=0.5u
.param W_xm6=5u L_xm6=0.5u

XM1 N0 LABEL_NET_0 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 N1 LABEL_NET_1 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 N1 N0 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM4 N0 N2 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}
XM5 N1 N2 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm5} w={W_xm5}
XM6 N0 N1 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm6} w={W_xm6}

VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VN2 N2 0 0.9
VIN_P LABEL_NET_0 0 PULSE(0 1.8 0 100p 100p 1.9n 4n)
VIN_N LABEL_NET_1 0 PULSE(1.8 0 0 100p 100p 1.9n 4n)

C0 N0 0 50f
C1 N1 0 50f

.control
tran 10p 20n

* Measure propagation delay
meas tran delay_fall trig v(LABEL_NET_0) val=0.9 rise=2 targ v(N0) val=0.9 fall=2
meas tran delay_rise trig v(LABEL_NET_0) val=0.9 fall=2 targ v(N0) val=0.9 rise=2
let tpd = (delay_fall + delay_rise) / 2
print tpd

* Measure output voltage swing
meas tran v_max max v(N0)
meas tran v_min min v(N0)
let v_swing = v_max - v_min
print v_swing

* Measure average power consumption
meas tran power_avg avg i(VVDD) from=4n to=16n
let power_mw = -power_avg * 1.8 * 1000
print power_mw

quit
.endc
.end
